terms.gloss: spare time, odd hours left over from work
terms.grammar: subsicīvus, subsicīva, subsicīvum, adjective, with tempus, temporis n.
evidence: Cic. Leg. 1.9: subsicīva quaedam tempora incurrunt, quae ego perīre nōn patior (Lewis & Short)
Plin. Ep. 3.15.1: aliquid subsicīvī temporis (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 109: cum tempus subsicīvum mihi est
terms.comment: A land surveyor’s word: subsicīvum is the strip left over when fields are divided, and so the hours left over from business.
Classically līberum tempus is time free of obligation (Lewis & Short); the phrase is Traupman’s everyday “free time”.
Ōtium mihi nōn erat, I didn’t have time; sī ōtium tibi est, if you have time.

phrases.latin: quantumque ā tuendā rē familiārī prōcūrandōque cultū līberōrum meōrum dabitur ōtium, ea omnia subsicīva et subsecundāria tempora ad colligendās hujuscemodī memoriārum dēlectātiunculās cōnferam
phrases.english: whatever leisure is left me from managing my household and seeing to my children’s education, all that spare time I shall give to collecting little pleasures of this kind for remembering

phrases.latin: Ostende mihi pecus, quaesō, sī ōtium tibi est.
phrases.english: Please show me your livestock, if you have time.

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
